text:
Abigail: Quick follow-up from today’s all-hands infra section. Capturing asks on APAC warmup parity, visible fallbacks, and procurement for Q3. Who's owning what? :wave:

Samir: APAC saw a lot of short-request cold starts last week (~2x). Can we get parity with US/EMEA prefill windows or a different schedule?

Elena: Rolling plan: increase APAC warm pool by ~30% for an 8-week experiment and add schedule-aware TTLs. Canary in apac-sg now.

Jon: What success metrics should product/eng watch?

Elena: Primary signals: prewarm_kv_hit_rate, p95_cold_infer_latency, and queue_depth_spike. Targets: hit_rate >= 0.9, p95_cold <= 250ms for <256-token calls.

Maya: Is this manually adjusted or automated? Ops had to intervene during last spike.

Elena: We're deploying prewarm-autoscaler v0.9. It uses a 5m sliding window + short-term forecast and a schedule layer for TTL changes. Canary tag: prewarm-autoscaler:canary-apac.

ops-bot: deploy 1759999980: prewarm-autoscaler v0.9 rolled to apac-sg canary :rocket:

Anya: For Dedicated customers with SLA commits, we must guarantee warm pools tied to their reserved capacity, not rely on shared prefill.

Infra-Lead: Confirmed. Dedicated customers get fixed warm pools behind reserve. Shared prewarm remains an optimization for public fleets.

Samir: If APAC saturates, do we prefer a local quantized fallback or cross-region routing to EMEA? Need clear behavior for latency-sensitive apps.

Elena: Routing policy v3: prefer same-region full_precision -> same-region quantized -> neighboring-region quantized -> fallback_region full_precision. We will emit fallback_region and fallback_type metrics.

Jon: Example snippet for docs/help center:
```
- policy: region_preference
  steps:
    - try: same_region.full_precision
    - try: same_region.quantized
    - try: neighboring_region.quantized
    - try: fallback_region.full_precision
```

Maya: Request: surface per-route fallback counts and average added latency in Console so customers can see cross-region or quantized fallbacks.

Infra-Lead: Owner: Jon -> console-metrics. ETA: 2 weeks. Ticket: INF-4210.

Abigail: Procurement ask from execs: finance needs recommended committed GPU counts for Q3 by end of month. Anya, can you lead modeling?

Anya: Yes. I'll run base/likely/peak scenarios and share a spreadsheet Monday. Engineering: please post 95th-percentile sustained GPU-hours by region by Friday.

Samir: Will provide APAC & EMEA 95th-percentiles. Also, for pricing, are we recommending annual commits or monthly flex?

Anya: Annual preferred for discounting; will include a monthly-flex option in the model. Recommendation included on the sheet.

Jon: Suggestion: extend warm TTL to 20m during APAC local peak windows. Thoughts?

Maya: +1 for local peaks. Need off-peak scale-down policy to avoid cost spikes.

Elena: Implemented schedule rules in canary: TTL=20m during APAC local peak window (00:00-12:00 UTC), TTL=10m otherwise. Dashboards updated.

ops-bot: alert: prewarm-autoscaler allocation +17% at 2024-08-02T09:12Z  monitoring.

Abigail: Action items recap: 1) Elena -> post dashboard links for prewarm_kv_hit_rate & p95_cold_infer_latency; 2) Jon -> add console fallback metrics (INF-4210); 3) Anya -> procurement spreadsheet + recommendation by Mon. I'll brief execs after Monday. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
